messages:
Alex Mora: @channel :rotating_light: PagerDuty triggered for SEV2 — potential cross-namespace routing observed. Incoming requests for ns-701 (Customer: Meridia Finance) are showing response headers referencing ns-902. I’m posting initial traces.
Oncall Bot: PagerDuty incident #PD-1129 opened for high-severity routing anomaly (rule: routing-namespace-mismatch). Assigned to oncall: Sara Kim.
Sara Kim: taking this on. Can someone paste the first suspicious trace ID?
Alex Mora: trace=trc-7f9b2. snippet from gateway logs:
```
[2026-03-15T03:24:10Z] req_id=trc-7f9b2 src=10.40.12.18 pool=dp-17 ns=ns-701 -> backend=svc-gen-1 (routed_to_ns=ns-902) headers={x-client-id:ns-902, x-auth-method:token}
```
Matt (ops): Confirmed. I’m seeing 12 requests in the last 5m where `routed_to_ns` != `ns` (origin). All from dp-17 (dedicated pool for region-us-east-2).
Priya (eng-sre): running `routedump --pool dp-17 --since 10m --json | jq '.[] | select(.routed_to_ns != .ns)'` now. Initial output matches the 12 entries.
DevSec Bot: Quick check: no suspicious outbound external egress seen. Connections are still internal to our infra. :eyes:
Sara Kim: Good. Priority now: 1) isolate customer traffic to prevent further cross-routing 2) identify the config change that introduced regression 3) assess customer impact (requests, potential header leakage)
Lina (CS): I’m opening a calm notify to Meridia Finance with limited details that we’re investigating a routing configuration issue and we will update in 1 hour. No need to escalate to legal yet.
Alex Mora: Suggested immediate mitigation: put dp-17 into quarantine mode (reject new routing decisions, serve static 503 to new sessions) and fail open to fallback pool for unaffected customers.
Matt (ops): executing quarantine: `infractl pool quarantine dp-17 --reason "routing-mismatch" --by oncall` -> accepted. New session handoffs now returning 503 for dp-17.
Priya (eng-sre): rolling routing-table rollback to previous commit (rfe-322-hotfix) that touched `prefix-mapping-service`. Hash: `a3f9c1d` -> executing rollout to region-us-east-2.
Sara Kim: while rollback runs, what evidence of actual data exposure? Any auth tokens or PII leaked in logs?
Alex Mora: so far we see `x-client-id` and `x-org` values belonging to other namespaces present in backend responses. No full bearer tokens in stored logs; ephemeral headers were truncated by gateway scrubber for stored logs. We need to check in-flight traces for any payload crossover.
Matt (ops): I pulled one raw trace from the stream (not stored): it shows an `Authorization` header for ns-902 present in an upstream call initiated while processing ns-701 request. That means short-lived header propagation happened between service-to-service call within the pool.
DevSec Bot: Immediate action: rotate internal service tokens used by dp-17 sidecar auth proxy and invalidate cached KV for prefix mapping. Command: `authctl rotate --scope pool:dp-17 --notify internal` executed.
Lina (CS): Notifying Meridia Finance again: we’ve quarantined the pool and started rotating internal tokens. We’re not seeing evidence of exfil of customer payloads, but we’ll confirm and share findings in 2 hours.
Sara Kim: handover — I need to go for 30m. @Matt (ops) you take primary, @Priya continue rollback verification, @Alex run impact audit. I’ll be reachable.
Matt (ops): taking over. Current mitigation status: dp-17 quarantined, internal tokens rotated, rollback to `a3f9c1d` at 03:29Z completed on 3/5 nodes, remaining 2 nodes draining.
Priya (eng-sre): rollback fully applied at 03:33Z. After rollback, routing logs show `routed_to_ns` == `ns` for new requests. I’m running a full mapping audit: `python tools/prefix_audit.py --pool dp-17 --out /tmp/audit-dp17.json` (will paste summary)
Alex Mora: audit summary (partial): total requests examined=2,400 window=1h; misrouted=23 unique requests; affected customers observed: ns-701 (Meridia Finance) and ns-902 (internal test account). No evidence of cross-customer payload retention in S3 or log buckets. Potential exposure vector: in-memory header propagation on the worker that had stale prefix-map cache.
DevSec Bot: Recommend follow-ups: 1) force cache invalidation across all pools (`cachectl invalidate prefix-map --all`) 2) add stricter scrubbing on inter-service headers 3) schedule rollout of header-sanitizer middleware.
Matt (ops): running cache invalidation now. `cachectl invalidate prefix-map --all` -> 0:03:40 elapsed -> success.
Lina (CS): Meridia update: thanks for quick action. They asked for concrete timeline for remediation and whether they should rotate any customer-side keys. I recommended we own rotation for anything internal and advise them only if we find customer tokens in logs. No customer rotation recommended yet.
Sara Kim: back online. Quick check: Are there any other pools with similar prefix-mapping versions? We should run a scanning query across Dedicated pools.
Priya (eng-sre): scanning now: `infractl list-pools --filter 'prefix-map-version>=a3f9c1d' | xargs -n1 sh -c 'infractl pool show $0'` — found 4 pools with the regressed binary; we’ve scheduled hotfix rollout to them (low risk hotpatch).
Alex Mora: root cause hypothesis: an automated config-reconciliation job that applies `legacy-prefix` patch merged incorrectly for dedicated pools only; it updated in-memory prefix map without invalidating caches. When a worker served a request after partial deploy, it used stale mapping and forwarded to wrong namespace. The change was included in commit `rfe-322` pushed earlier this morning.
DevSec Bot: classification: Security incident - potential data exposure. Severity remains SEV2 because we have confirmed cross-namespace header propagation but no persisted exfil confirmed. Notify Security and Compliance.
Matt (ops): Opened internal security notification and created SJ-540 (security investigation).
Lina (CS): Meridia Finance wants a timeline for postmortem and remediation steps. I promised an initial incident summary within 8 hours and full RCA within 72 hours.
Sara Kim: Next operational tasks (owners):
- Priya: complete hotpatch rollout to the 4 affected pools and run mapping audit (ETA 45m)
- Alex: full payload audit for last 24h for ns-701 + ns-902 (ETA 2h)
- Matt: coordinate with Security to triage raw traces and stash evidence (ETA 1h)
- Lina: customer comms and legal sync (ongoing)
DevSec Bot: add automated guard: commit hook added to prevent `prefix-map` changes without `cache-invalidate` call; CI job created: `ci/guard-prefix-invalidate`.
Alex Mora: quick note on mitigation completeness: we rotated internal tokens and invalidated caches, rolled back the regressed commit, quarantined the affected pool. Postfix checks show routing returning to normal and no new misroutes after 03:34Z.
Priya (eng-sre): audit finished: misrouted unique requests = 23, distinct payloads touched = 3 (internal test payloads), customer-PII not found. Uploading audit artifact to secure bucket `s3://redwood-incidents/PD-1129/audit-summary.txt` (access: security, eng-sre, cs).
Sara Kim: closing notes: incident transitioned to mitigation -> monitoring. We’ll keep thread open for the RCA. Great work team. :thumbsup:
Lina (CS): I notified Meridia Finance with the summary and ETA for RCA. They requested dedicated follow-up call — scheduled for 2026-03-15T11:00Z.
Matt (ops): closing the on-call handoff to overnight team with summary in PagerDuty. If anything pops, page priority=high.
Oncall Bot: Incident #PD-1129 status updated: Mitigated -> Monitoring. Incident will auto-close after 72h with no regressions.
Sara Kim: thanks everyone. RCA owners will post follow-up in #postmortems.
